rows.title: Auto-Fix turns 'Worked with <people>' into 'Engineered <people>'
rows.summary: Now: 'worked with' is its own weak-phrase entry. Auto-Fix writes 'Collaborated with product managers to define the roadmap', and the tip offers 'Collaborated with' or 'Partnered with'. 'Worked on' still becomes 'Engineered'. The ATS weak-phrase list is unchanged because it reads the same entries.

rows.title: Present-tense bullets for a current job ('Manage', 'Develop', 'Lead', 'Build') count as having no action verb
rows.summary: Now: leadsWithActionVerb also counts a word whose past tense is a listed verb (word+ed/d, doubled consonant, y to ied, plus a small irregular table: lead/led, build/built, run/ran, grow/grew, oversee/oversaw and others). The ATS score, the optimizer badge and the chip all read it. 'Manage a team of 8...' shows a verb, three present-tense bullets score 'Strong Action Verbs (100%)', and a chip gives 'Spearheaded a team of 8...'. Every starter bullet, the academic starter's 'Lead the lab...' and 'Mentor two doctoral students...' included, now opens with a known verb. These are not counted, so a chip goes in front of them and no word is lost: a word that often opens a noun or title (design, test, engineer, head, double and others); a present form followed by a preposition or punctuation ('Mentor to 5 interns', 'Chair, ACM'); and 'Lead <title>' ('Lead engineer for...'). 'Take part in' is treated like 'Took part in'.

rows.title: A power-verb chip on 'Maintained compliance with...', 'Active member of...' or 'Supported delivery of...' deletes the noun as well
rows.summary: Now: the chip replaces a whole phrase only when it is a verb plus its preposition or particle ('Contributed to', 'Collaborated on', 'Led efforts to', 'Took part in'). Otherwise it replaces just the verb: 'Maintained compliance with HIPAA' becomes 'Streamlined compliance with HIPAA', and 'Supported delivery of...' becomes 'Architected delivery of...' ('supported' is added to ACTION_VERBS because the tips offer it). 'Member of...' and 'Active member of...' say no action, so the chip leaves them unchanged and the modal asks for a rewrite, as it does for a leading helper verb.

issues: R5-HUNT10-PRESENT-TENSE-VERBS-NOT-ACTION-VERBS: the title check ran only after 'Lead', so 'Support engineer for the payments team' and 'Build engineer on the CI team' counted as a present verb, and a chip deleted the word: 'Spearheaded engineer for the payments team'. 'support' became a listed verb in 55bf7e1a, which made the 'Support engineer' case reachable. Fixed: one singular title (engineer, specialist, lead, agent and others) after any present form makes it a role that is not counted. A plural is still the verb's object ('Manage engineers', 'Support analysts').

R5-HUNT10-PRESENT-TENSE-VERBS-NOT-ACTION-VERBS: the preposition guard also caught verbs that are never nouns. 'Contribute to open-source projects' and 'Collaborate on the SDK' read 'Verb Missing' and scored no verb, though 'Contributed to...' counts, and a chip left 'Spearheaded Contribute to open-source projects', the same doubled verb the fix was for. Fixed: these two count as verbs, and a chip replaces the whole phrase ('Spearheaded open-source projects'), as it does for the past tense.
review.notes: The fixer's failfirst run 36653304179 is green: each of the 3 tests failed with its src diff reversed (fail 3 for the present-tense test) and passed with the fix restored. The root causes are right: 'worked with' has its own entry, whole-phrase replacement is limited to a verb plus its preposition, and present forms are found through the past-tense list. Nothing outside src/utils/bulletOptimizer.js is touched, and no stored data or sync is involved. The ATS score still counts at most one weak phrase per bullet. The optimizer now takes 15 points off twice for a bullet with both 'worked on' and 'worked with', which is two weak phrases. My run 36653918942: failfirst for 45b31bb5 is green (fail 2 without the fix, pass with it); 334/334 node tests across bullet-optimizer*, *ats*, r4-lo-1*, r4-sw-wt-0*, r5-hunt9-*verb*, r5-opt-sw-wt-0*, r5-hunt10-*, knowledge-docs, and pdf 104-verb-chip, 77, 76, 56, 98-ats-claims; Cypress 28-writing-helpers 4/4; lint green. Every starter bullet still opens with a verb that counts. Open follow-ups, not fixed here. They are the chip design's existing behaviour for a verb that takes a preposition, in any tense. (1) A chip on a verb before 'with' keeps the 'with': 'Collaborated with PMs' becomes 'Spearheaded with PMs'. This existed before for 'Partnered with', and Auto-Fix and the tips now write 'Collaborated/Partnered/Coordinated/Liaised with', so it will come up more often. It needs a design decision: keep 'with' only for chip verbs that take it (Partnered, Liaised, Coordinated), and otherwise ask for a rewrite. (2) 'Worked with React and Node' is changed by Auto-Fix to 'Collaborated with React and Node', because 'worked with' followed by a tool is not a collaboration. Before, it read 'Engineered React and Node'. (3) Present forms before at/for/on stay uncounted as a safe choice ('Speak at meetups', 'Present at conferences', 'Teach at a bootcamp'): the chip goes in front of them and no word is lost. The past tense ('Spoke at meetups') takes the chip in place of the verb, which gives 'Spearheaded at meetups'. (4) Some noun-led openers that are also common verbs still count as a verb, and a chip drops the noun: 'Build times cut by 40%' becomes 'Spearheaded times cut by 40%', and 'Mentor program lead' has the same problem. It is the opposite trade-off to 'Build dashboards'. No accessibility issues seen.
